pitch: Sparky 3000 ate Dex Dynamo's science report: find 20 pages across the suburbs, the clouds, the Superhighway, the Mega Mall and the Moon before the Science Fair at 3:00. Bring a quarter!

keys.Space: Fire the Laser-Tag Zapper (find it in your backyard first)
keys.F2: Status: score, lives, hit points and quarters in your pocket

items.title: In The Year 2000 Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck in the future? Find your question, then lay the red film over the answer. Read only the one you need: the Science Fair starts at 3:00 sharp!

hints.a: In your own backyard, north of the garage wall. You need the garage remote to open the GATE CLICK door first.
In the hedge garden at the bottom left of the neighborhood. Squeeze in through the gaps in the hedges; a robo-mower guards it.
Not the OUT one, and not the one that just rings. The working booth is in the far right corner, past the newspaper cannons. Keep a quarter for it!

hints.q: Can I zap the hoverboard kids?
hints.a: No. They zoom up and down the roads, so look both ways and cross behind them.

hints.q: How do I drive this thing?
hints.a: You don't: Grandpa's CitiCar flies itself. Left and Right (or A and D) steer it one whole lane at a time. Up and Down do nothing up here.

Everything comes out of the middle of the horizon as a dot, then slides into its lane. Watch which way the dot drifts, and move as soon as you know. When two lanes are blocked, the third is clear, and often has a page in it.
Watch the sign: SKYWAY 9 MI counts down a mile every six seconds. At 0 MI the exit ramp lights up over the RIGHT lane. Be in the right lane and the car takes the ramp by itself.
Dinner pills come down the lanes too. Steer into one for a turkey dinner.

hints.q: How do I cross fourteen lanes of traffic?
hints.a: Island by island. Wait on a deck for a gap, then dash. Gold trucks are slow, red cars are medium, and the teal cars are VERY fast.
At the far right of the last platform at the bottom, past the FAX-A-PIZZA billboard. The one next to where you start is out of order.

hints.q: What does the glass tube do?
hints.a: It whisks you along to the right in a hurry. Step off the side if you want to grab a page instead.

hints.q: How do I get the STAFF ONLY keycard?
hints.a: It's in the corner of TV-RAMA behind a laser fence. Stand next to the lasers and walk through as soon as they blink off. They stay off three times longer than they stay on.

hints.q: Where is the STAFF ONLY door?
hints.a: On the south wall of the concourse, on the right. The loading dock behind it has three more laser fences and the phone booth.

hints.q: Are the arcade games worth it?
hints.a: Arcade games give 1,000 points and pinball gives 2,500, but each one eats a quarter and then it's GAME OVER. Never spend your last quarter!

hints.q: The security robots keep catching me.
hints.a: They are slower than you are. Lead them in a loop, then turn around and zap them.

Booth 3 is the shortest way: inside a TV set, then the Jurassic period, then the Moon Shuttle launch pad. Booths 1 and 2 work too, they just take the scenic route. (The teletype in the corner has been trying to tell you.)
Every room has quarters, and they come back every time you dial into it. Pick them up before you dial again.

hints.q: How do I get on the Moon Shuttle?
hints.a: Walk up the boarding ramp right under the rocket. It's chained off while the countdown runs (6, 5, 4...): wait for its board to say GO. The booth on the launch pad only takes you back to the hall.
Booth 1 goes to Grandma's condo in Florida. She gives a big hug that heals you.
At the top left of the Moon, west of the big dome. Hop up meteor alley to get it.

hints.q: How do I dodge the meteors?
hints.a: They fall at a slant from the sky along the top edge. Watch where they land, then hop through behind them.
The base at the top right. Walk into the MOON PASS airlock with the pass, and the door to the Science Fair is inside.
Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: he roams, then plays keep-away (corner him), then gets the zoomies. Then he gets dizzy and drops the cover page.

You zapped it. A zap burns the cover page up, so stop firing once Sparky drops it. The school keeps one spare cover, on the floor right beside the copier at the bottom of the gym: walk into it. There is only the one.

hints.q: What do I do at the judges' table?
hints.a: Walk into the table with 20 pages to turn them in, then walk into the COVER table behind it with the cover page. Then step up to the podium!
The lava blobs wander slowly. Keep moving, and grab a food pill if you get singed.

hints.q: What's in the closet next to the launch pad?
hints.a: Some say the felt-maker left something behind. In the future not every brick is a brick.
It doesn't need one. Look along the Moon Shuttle pad's right wall for a brick with teal light glowing through its mortar.

On the Moon Shuttle pad, get into the row of the boarding ramp, on the ramp's right side (don't step on the ramp itself, or you're off to the Moon). Walk right into the glowing brick: you walk straight through it. Press G to pick up the felt egg, then walk on into the rocket hatch at the far end.

items.title: The Hover Heights Herald
items.headline: IT'S THE YEAR 2000!
items.deck: Cars fly, robots mow, dinner fits in a pill; local robot dog eats science report

photo.caption: The Dynamo family dome on Dome Circle. Robots mowed this lawn.

columns: HOVER HEIGHTS - The new millennium arrived right on time last night, and so did everything else. Flying cars filled the Information Superhighway by breakfast. Robo-mowers trimmed every lawn in neat little squares.

Dinner, as everybody always said it would, now comes in a pill. "It tastes just like turkey," said one diner. "With stuffing."

The aliens next door report that they are having a lovely time and would like a hug.

One family was not celebrating. Sparky 3000, a robot dog, reportedly ate a twenty-page science report titled The Pocket Telephone. "A telephone in your POCKET?" laughed one neighbor. "What'll they think of next?"
briefs: Computers everywhere woke up fine. The only bug in Hover Heights was a robot dog.
Still 25 cents a call. Booth 4 at the exchange is out of order again.
Sunny. Meteor showers this afternoon. Bring a helmet.

news.head: Our second game: In The Year 2000!
news.html: Sandbox Software is three months old, and its second game is in your hands. In In The Year 2000! you are Dex Dynamo, age 11, and your robot dog Sparky 3000 just ate your science report. Find 20 pages across six levels of the future, from the dome homes of Hover Heights to the Moon, and get them to the Science Fair by 3:00. Bring a quarter: every phone booth is a Teleport-A-Phone.

news.head: What will the year 2000 be like?
news.html: We asked our classmates what they expect in seven short years. The top answers: flying cars (41 votes), robot dogs (29), dinner in a pill (17), and a telephone small enough to fit in your pocket (2 votes, and one of those was a joke). Our programmer is betting on the pocket telephone. Our mail room is still betting on the mail.

news.head: Sparky says thanks
news.html: Register In The Year 2000! for $12 and you get the next Sandbox Software game on a 3 1/2" disk, a printed manual and a sticker for your computer. Sparky promises not to eat any of it.

news.head: Since last issue: Snowbound, rough edges and all
news.html: Snowbound got our roughest reviews and our warmest letters. Yes, it’s the simplest game we’ll ever make; it’s also the truest. Readers from all over Mineral County wrote to say we got the sled run on Jamie Street just right. The most-asked question: does the arcade eat all your dollars? Only if you let it. Count the can (F2) before you head for the register.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Homework comes first
news.html: The founder is a junior at Frankfort High, so Sandbox Software keeps strict hours: after homework, before bed, and all day Saturday. The office is still a desk, the family 286 and a stack of graph paper. The snow shovel has moved to the porch. It may be needed again.

news.head: In the workshop: A puzzle made of pure Game-Maker
news.html: The founder's notebook is already full. First on the list is a puzzle game where electricity is made of ordinary Game-Maker blocks and monsters: switches, fuses, and a little robot who must never touch a live wire. Its working title is Ohm Sweet Ohm, and we apologize for it now. It won’t be quick: there’s homework first, and a diploma after that.

news.head: Letters: "Did you make it to the mall?"
news.html:
"In Snowbound, did the real founder make it to the register in time?" - A reader in West Virginia

The Scoop replies: Look at the name on this newsletter. Then look at the box your game came in.
